narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m1'/>Many numbers work, because most nine digit numbers get bigger after some swap.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But we need every swap to make it bigger, and not only some swaps.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>A single swap that makes it smaller breaks the number, and the slip is struck out.
removed_beats.on_screen: the slip's bubble appears with many numbers; the word every glows; the slip is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Think about what a swap does to the left digit.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Climbing digits are the only ones that always grow.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Count by checking what choices are left.
removed_beats.on_screen: the words left digit appear; the words climbing digits appear; the words count the choices appear

old_misconception.wrong_move: A common slip thinks many numbers work. All the digits must be different and must climb, so only one number remains.
